newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends steady to down, eyes on gasoline.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends steady to down, eyes on gasoline.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended steady to slightly lower as traders zeroed in on gasoline's volatility as the key to demand for the heavier naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) material.
June swaps finished $1 lower at $178.50/$179.50 after rising to $181/$182 with the early rebound in crude futures. July swaps moved into a minor backwardation, ending at $178.25/$179.50.

One trader said the sharp drop in gasoline over the last week had narrowed the spread to naphtha prices so much it was not economical for reformers to buy the heavier material. N+A is used as a feedstock to make gasoline and, he said, should normally yield a $20 discount.
"Reforming is no longer economical for refiners," he said. "I agree it is difficult to find high quality N+A...but from my point of view it is overvalued."
He said the cargo market appeared tighter, likely due to material recently shipped out to Brazil and Japan.
Naphtha stocks in the 15 countries of the European Union plus Norway fell by 1.76 million barrels in May to 25.96 million, Stitching Euroilstock said.
